headline: HC confirms death sentence for rape and murder of 8-year-old Asiya
summary: The High Court upheld the death penalty for Hitu Sheikh, ruling that the crime was heinous and the convict deserves the maximum punishment.
details: The High Court has confirmed the death sentence of Hitu Sheikh, the lone convict in the case regarding the rape and murder of eight-year-old Asiya in Magura last year.
A bench of Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja delivered the verdict after dismissing the appeals filed by Hitu Sheikh and accepting the death reference.
The court stated that the incident was a very heinous crime and that there was no doubt Hitu Sheikh committed the act, thus deserving the maximum punishment.
On May 17 last year, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal in Magura had initially sentenced Hitu Sheikh to death.
The victim, Asiya, had visited her elder sister's in-laws' home in Nijnanduali Mathpara, Magura Sadar, on March 1 last year.
She was raped in the early hours of March 6 last year and was taken to Magura 250-bed District Hospital in critical condition.
Asiya was later transferred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital and then to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, and finally to the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka, where she died on March 13.
Hitu Sheikh's wife, Jaheda Begum, and their sons Ratul Sheikh and Sajib Sheikh, other accused in the case, were acquitted as charges against them could not be proven.
caption:
A heinous crime against an 8-year-old child. The High Court has upheld the death sentence for the convict.

The High Court has confirmed the death sentence of Hitu Sheikh, the lone convict in the case regarding the rape and murder of eight-year-old Asiya in Magura last year.

A bench of Justice Bhishmadev Chakrabortty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja delivered the verdict after dismissing the appeals filed by Hitu Sheikh and accepting the death reference.

The court stated that the incident was a very heinous crime and that there was no doubt Hitu Sheikh committed the act, thus deserving the maximum punishment.

On May 17 last year, the Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal in Magura had initially sentenced Hitu Sheikh to death.

The victim, Asiya, had visited her elder sister's in-laws' home in Nijnanduali Mathpara, Magura Sadar, on March 1 last year.

She was raped in the early hours of March 6 last year and was taken to Magura 250-bed District Hospital in critical condition.

Asiya was later transferred to Faridpur Medical College Hospital and then to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, and finally to the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka, where she died on March 13.

Hitu Sheikh's wife, Jaheda Begum, and their sons Ratul Sheikh and Sajib Sheikh, other accused in the case, were acquitted as charges against them could not be proven.

headline_marked: US provides [[$2.4m health equipment]] to Bangladesh
headline: US provides $2.4m health equipment to Bangladesh
summary: The aid focuses on strengthening maternal, newborn, and child healthcare services across the country, including remote areas.
details: The United States is providing medical equipment and materials worth $2.4 million (approximately 29.32 crore BDT) to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of Bangladesh.
The assistance aims to strengthen maternal, newborn, and child healthcare services throughout the country.
US Ambassador Brent T. Christensen handed over training models for maternal and newborn health services to Civil Surgeon Dr. Mo. Mizanur Rahman at Panchagarh District Hospital.
The aid includes equipment for keeping newborns warm, respiratory support tools, therapeutic food for severely malnourished children, and materials to maintain vaccine efficacy.
These supplies are being delivered to hospitals and health centers nationwide, including in remote areas, through FHI 360, JPGO, JSI, and UNICEF.
The initiative is part of the 'America First Global Health Strategy' to strengthen health systems through practical partnerships and advance US health sector innovation.
The US Embassy stated that it remains committed to working with the Bangladesh government to expand access to quality healthcare services across the country.
caption:
The US is donating $2.4 million in medical equipment to boost maternal and child health services in Bangladesh.

The United States is providing medical equipment and materials worth $2.4 million (approximately 29.32 crore BDT) to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare of Bangladesh.

The assistance aims to strengthen maternal, newborn, and child healthcare services throughout the country.

US Ambassador Brent T. Christensen handed over training models for maternal and newborn health services to Civil Surgeon Dr. Mo. Mizanur Rahman at Panchagarh District Hospital.

The aid includes equipment for keeping newborns warm, respiratory support tools, therapeutic food for severely malnourished children, and materials to maintain vaccine efficacy.

These supplies are being delivered to hospitals and health centers nationwide, including in remote areas, through FHI 360, JPGO, JSI, and UNICEF.

The initiative is part of the 'America First Global Health Strategy' to strengthen health systems through practical partnerships and advance US health sector innovation.

The US Embassy stated that it remains committed to working with the Bangladesh government to expand access to quality healthcare services across the country.
